items.title: Rank market scanner hits by confluence and risk quality
items.body:
## Problem

`/api/webhook/market-scanner-alert` currently reports scanner results in the order returned by each TradingView MCP scan, with only light per-section filtering/formatting. It does not compute a cross-signal score, deduplicate the same symbol across scans, or highlight the strongest risk-adjusted setups first.

That means a raw top gainer or high-volume move can appear as prominently as a cleaner setup with aligned volume, RSI, breakout direction, and recommendation context.

## Trading Hypothesis

Ranking scanner hits by confluence and risk quality should reduce noisy alerts and make the scanner output more useful for trade triage. This is a signal-quality improvement only; it does not imply guaranteed profit.

## Proposed Change

Add a deterministic scanner scoring layer before report formatting:

- compute `signalScore` for each scanner item using available fields such as `changePercent`, `volume_ratio`, `breakout_type`, RSI, `trading_recommendation`, and Bollinger width
- add `setupType` and `riskFlags` fields for explainability
- deduplicate symbols that appear in multiple scans and preserve scan-source metadata
- either sort each section by `signalScore` or add a top `MEJORES SETUPS` section while preserving legacy sections
- expose scores in dry-run/API responses so ranking can be tested without sending notifications

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Market scanner items receive a deterministic `signalScore` and human-readable reason list.
- [ ] Duplicate symbols across scans are merged or clearly linked instead of repeated blindly.
- [ ] Scanner report output prioritizes stronger confluence without hiding partial scan failures.
- [ ] Unit tests cover scoring, dedupe, and stable ordering for representative gainers, volume breakout, smart volume, and Bollinger items.
- [ ] Integration tests cover `dryRun` output and preserve `validateApiKey`, feature gating, idempotency, and fail-open scan behavior.
- [ ] If the request/response contract changes, `src/openapi/openapi.json` and `CabrosBot.postman_collection.json` are updated.

## Validation Plan

- Add deterministic fixtures under scanner report/unit tests.
- Run focused tests for `marketScannerReport` and market-scanner endpoint.
- Validate a dry-run payload with mixed scans and repeated symbols.
- Roll out as report-only ranking first; do not change notification routing or auth.

## Evidence

- `src/services/tradingview/marketScannerReport.js:26` defaults to `top_gainers`, `top_losers`, and `volume_breakout_scanner`, leaving stronger context scans optional.
- `src/services/tradingview/marketScannerReport.js:180-224` iterates `scanResults` and `itemsToRender` in existing order with no scoring/ranking layer.
- `src/services/tradingview/marketScannerReport.js:230-253` formats only raw per-item fields like RSI, volume ratio, breakout direction, or BBW.
- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/marketScanner/marketScanner.js:169-219` runs each scan and stores raw `items` without normalizing a cross-scan signal model.
- Related issues/PRs: no open PRs and no open/closed issue matches found for scanner ranking/confluence dedupe.

## Risks

- A naive score could overfit noisy indicators. Keep the scoring deterministic, explainable, covered by fixtures, and initially observable through dry-run/report output.
- Preserve existing protected webhook auth, feature gate, MarkdownV2-compatible text, and fail-open scan handling.

items.title: Agregar pruebas automatizadas (unitarias e integracion)
items.body:
## Problema
El proyecto no tiene **ningun test automatizado**. Esto hace que cambios en scrapers puedan romperse sin ser detectados, errores de regresion pasen desapercibidos, y sea dificil contribuir sin miedo a romper algo.

## A quien afecta
Desarrolladores y mantenedores del bot.

## Cambio propuesto
Agregar suite de tests con `pytest`:

1. **Unitarios para `filters/discount_filter.py`**: `compute_discount_percentage()`, `filter_products()`, `_keyword_matches()`, `_looks_like_accessory_or_related()`, `boost_cross_store_scores()`
2. **Unitarios para `services/subscription_parser.py`**: parseo de `/watch` con opciones, errores
3. **Unitarios para `utils/normalization.py`**: `fix_text_encoding()`, `normalize_product_name()`
4. **Tests con mocks para scrapers**: `_parse_next_data_products()`, `_product_from_search_item()`

## Criterios de aceptacion
- [ ] `pytest` funciona sin conexion a internet (mocks)
- [ ] Cobertura minima 70% en modulos de logica pura
- [ ] Tests se ejecutan en CI (GitHub Actions)
- [ ] `pytest` y `pytest-cov` agregados a `requirements.txt`

## Evidencia
- `requirements.txt` no incluye pytest
- No existen archivos `test_*.py`
- `filters/discount_filter.py` tiene logica pura sin dependencias externas

items.title: Permitir pausar y editar suscripciones existentes
items.body:
## Problema
Actualmente los usuarios solo pueden **crear** o **eliminar** suscripciones. No hay forma de pausar temporalmente una suscripcion sin perderla, ni editar el descuento minimo, keywords, o label de una existente. Esto fuerza al usuario a eliminar y recrear, perdiendo el historial.

## A quien afecta
A todos los usuarios del bot.

## Cambio propuesto
1. Agregar comando `/pause <id>` y opcion en menu para pausar/reanudar
2. Agregar comando `/edit <id>` y/o flujo conversacional para editar campos
3. Soporte en `SupabaseRepository` para actualizar suscripcion
4. Nuevos botones: "Pausar alerta", "Reanudar alerta", "Editar alerta"

## Criterios de aceptacion
- [ ] Usuario puede pausar una suscripcion desde el menu
- [ ] Usuario puede reanudar una suscripcion pausada
- [ ] Usuario puede editar `min_discount` y `exclude_keywords`
- [ ] Suscripciones pausadas no aparecen en `get_active_subscriptions()`
- [ ] Suscripciones editadas mantienen su `id` e historial de alertas

## Evidencia
- README: "el bot no tiene comandos de pausa/edicion todavia"
- `subscriptions` tiene columna `enabled` que permite toggle
- `get_active_subscriptions()` ya filtra por `enabled: eq.true`

items.title: Agregar scraper para Ripley
items.body:
## Problema
Actualmente el bot solo cubre **Paris**, **Lider** y **Falabella**. **Ripley** es una de las tiendas departamentales mas grandes de Chile y su ausencia deja fuera una fuente importante de ofertas para los usuarios.

## A quien afecta
A todos los usuarios que quieren recibir alertas de Ripley.

## Cambio propuesto
Agregar un scraper para Ripley (ripley.cl) siguiendo el mismo patron que los scrapers existentes:
- `scraper/ripley_scraper.py` con clase `RipleyScraper`
- Integrarlo en `services/alert_engine.py` junto a los otros scrapers
- Soportar busqueda por query y validacion de stock en PDP

## Criterios de aceptacion
- [ ] `_scrape_search_query()` devuelve productos con descuento desde Ripley
- [ ] `get_product_page_state()` valida disponibilidad y stock
- [ ] Productos incluyen store="ripley" para diferenciacion
- [ ] Los productos aparecen en alertas mezclados con las demas tiendas

## Evidencia
- Paris, Lider y Falabella comparten el mismo patron de implementacion
- Ripley usa Next.js igual que Falabella y Lider
- El `alert_engine.py` ya soporta agregar scrapers nuevos en el diccionario `scrapers`

## Issues/PRs relacionados
Ninguno

## Riesgos
- Ripley podria cambiar su estructura HTML/JSON
- Posible rate limiting

items.title: Fix render.yaml to point at the current repository and deployment contract
items.body:
## Problem
The checked-in `render.yaml` still points to `https://github.com/francovp/cabros-crypto-bot-telegram`, while this repository is `francovp/cabros-bot`.

## Why it matters
That breaks the IaC story for anyone trying to deploy from the current repo:
- Render blueprints can target the wrong source repository
- preview/prod deployments may drift from the code and docs being maintained here
- contributors cannot trust `render.yaml` as the canonical deployment contract

## Proposed change
Update `render.yaml` so it reflects the current repository and runtime setup:
- change `repo` to `https://github.com/francovp/cabros-bot`
- verify the service name still matches the intended product naming
- verify the env var contract in the blueprint covers the currently required boot path
- add a small validation step in docs or CI so future repo renames do not silently stale the blueprint again

## Acceptance criteria
- `render.yaml` points to `francovp/cabros-bot`
- blueprint deploys the same codebase that the README documents
- preview behavior remains correct for `IS_PULL_REQUEST`
- any remaining intentional divergence is documented in the repo

## Evidence
- repository under review: `francovp/cabros-bot`
- `render.yaml` currently contains `repo: https://github.com/francovp/cabros-crypto-bot-telegram`

## Related
- no open issues or PRs matched this deployment drift at review time

## Suggested labels
- bug
- devops
- deployment

items.title: Document and template WEBHOOK_API_KEY and missing runtime env vars
items.body:
## Problem
The runtime protects `/api` endpoints with `x-api-key` when `WEBHOOK_API_KEY` is configured, but `.env.example` does not document `WEBHOOK_API_KEY` at all. The same template also misses other runtime vars already referenced in the README, such as `ENABLE_FIRESTORE_JOB_STORAGE`, `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_SYMBOLS`, and `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_TIMEOUT_MS`.

## Why it matters
This creates avoidable onboarding friction and an easy security footgun:
- operators can deploy the service without realizing the webhook/API auth key exists
- teams following `.env.example` will miss feature flags that are already part of the documented API surface
- the README and env template drift makes production setup harder to trust

## Proposed change
Update `.env.example` so it matches the current runtime contract and README:
- add `WEBHOOK_API_KEY` with a clear note that it secures `/api/*` endpoints via the `x-api-key` header
- add the missing Firestore job-storage and expanded-analysis env vars already described in the README
- group the new vars in the same feature sections already used by the template
- add a short note in the README setup flow pointing out that `.env.example` is the canonical operator template

## Acceptance criteria
- `.env.example` includes `WEBHOOK_API_KEY`
- `.env.example` includes `ENABLE_FIRESTORE_JOB_STORAGE`
- `.env.example` includes `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_SYMBOLS`
- `.env.example` includes `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_TIMEOUT_MS`
- names/defaults/descriptions are aligned with the README and current code behavior
- setup docs no longer leave API auth undocumented

## Evidence
- `src/lib/auth.js` reads `process.env.WEBHOOK_API_KEY` and accepts `x-api-key`
- `README.md` states protected `/api` operations require `x-api-key`
- `.env.example` currently omits `WEBHOOK_API_KEY`
- `README.md` documents `ENABLE_FIRESTORE_JOB_STORAGE`, `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_SYMBOLS`, and `EXPANDED_ANALYSIS_ALERT_TIMEOUT_MS`, but `.env.example` does not

## Related
- no open issues or PRs matched this gap at review time

## Suggested labels
- documentation
- security
- developer-experience

---

**Linear**: [CB-35](https://linear.app/knil/issue/CB-35/document-and-template-webhook-api-key-and-missing-runtime-env-vars)

items.title: Handle Gemini quota exhaustion in production news monitoring

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: High-impact automation or platform reliability work

items.body:
## Production signal

Sentry project `hyrule-c7/cabros-bot` (`4510434640330752`), environment `production`.

New issue: https://hyrule-c7.sentry.io/issues/CABROS-BOT-B

Current window `2026-06-12T13:00:07Z` to `2026-06-20T22:03:41Z`:

- `2` Gemini `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` events, `1` impacted user
- First/last seen: `2026-06-19T09:19:24Z` / `2026-06-19T13:22:29Z`
- Transaction: `GET /api/news-monitor`
- Quota: `15 requests/minute/project/model`; provider retry delay: `30s`
- First-party frame: `src/services/grounding/genaiClient.js:218`
- Trace `d1b1da7aa3ad946b1392cd8cab1eea57`: `2315ms`, 8 Gemini spans
- Trace `0302fa1f1a63728a8d12fcebe0c47d23`: `4093ms`, 4 Gemini spans

Production `GET /api/news-monitor`: count `12`, avg `5078ms`, p95 `14610ms`, max `14875ms`. Previous equal-length window: **No measurements found**, so no percentage regression is claimed.

The analyzer fans symbols out in parallel. It converts per-symbol failures into `ANALYSIS_ERROR`, so the endpoint may return partial results while Sentry records provider exceptions.

## Dedupe

No open issue or open/closed PR matched `CABROS-BOT-B`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, Gemini quota, or this news-monitor failure.

Issue #81 / PR #85 cover Gemini `400 FAILED_PRECONDITION`, not quota exhaustion. No release tag was present, so this is not attributed to a specific commit.

## Fix direction

- Add configurable Gemini concurrency limiting to `NewsAnalyzer.analyzeSymbols()`.
- Treat `429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` as retryable; honor provider retry metadata with bounded jitter/backoff inside `NEWS_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- Fail open per symbol and expose quota-exhausted counts in response/Sentry context.
- Use another provider only when explicitly configured.

## Acceptance criteria

- Multi-symbol requests obey the configured Gemini concurrency limit.
- Mocked `429` responses retry within budget without uncaught provider exceptions.
- Other symbols complete with deterministic partial-failure details.
- Tests cover concurrency, retry exhaustion, timeout interaction, and configured fallback.
- `CABROS-BOT-B` receives no new production events after deploy.

---

**Linear**: [CB-34](https://linear.app/knil/issue/CB-34/handle-gemini-quota-exhaustion-in-production-news-monitoring)

items.title: Notify admin chat when delivery channels fail

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: High-impact automation or platform reliability work

items.body:
## Summary

Notify the admin Telegram chat when notification channel delivery fails after retries.

## Live evidence

- `README.md` documents `TELEGRAM_ADMIN_NOTIFICATIONS_CHAT_ID` for admin notifications and deployment alerts.
- `specs/002-whatsapp-alerts/spec.md` requires an admin notification when enabled channel retries are exhausted.
- `src/services/notification/NotificationManager.js` currently captures failed Telegram/WhatsApp delivery attempts with `SentryService.captureExternalFailure(...)`.
- The same implementation does not send a Telegram admin message when one or more enabled channels fail.

## Reliability impact

Sentry captures are useful for observability, but they are passive. For a notification bot, final delivery failure is itself a paging-worthy event: if WhatsApp or Telegram exhausts retries, operators should know in the admin chat without having to inspect Sentry.

## Proposal

- Add an admin notification path for final channel delivery failures after retry exhaustion.
- Send a compact message to `TELEGRAM_ADMIN_NOTIFICATIONS_CHAT_ID` when configured and Telegram is enabled.
- Include failed channel names, provider status/error, request/correlation ID when available, and whether other channels succeeded.
- Prevent loops: admin delivery failure should be logged/Sentry-captured but must not recursively trigger another admin notification.

## Acceptance criteria

- A simulated WhatsApp final failure triggers one Telegram admin notification when `TELEGRAM_ADMIN_NOTIFICATIONS_CHAT_ID` is configured.
- Partial failure still returns the existing webhook success response and still reports the failing channel in delivery results.
- If Telegram itself is the failed channel, the code does not recurse or block webhook completion.
- Unit or integration coverage verifies the admin notification behavior and the no-recursion guard.

## Dedupe check

Checked live open issues and PRs before filing. Targeted searches for admin notification delivery failures and `TELEGRAM_ADMIN_NOTIFICATIONS_CHAT_ID` returned no matching issue or PR.

---

**Linear**: [CB-33](https://linear.app/knil/issue/CB-33/notify-admin-chat-after-channel-delivery-failure)
